citations.summary:
I checked all 25 bullets in SEED.md §9 as 27 references: Witten 1983 is split into its two papers (NPB 223, 422 and 433), and so is Luhn-Nasri-Ramond (the J. Math. Phys. paper and the PLB paper). No repository files were created or changed.

ACCESS LIMITATION: I could not open any page directly. WebFetch failed with getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND for every host I tried (arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, inspirehep.net, api.crossref.org, en.wikipedia.org). Bash curl to the same hosts and to doi.org, journals.aps.org, ADS, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, projecteuclid, Springer, AIP and pdg.lbl.gov was refused by the egress proxy (CONNECT 403, a policy denial). So every result below rests on WebSearch result summaries: text the search tool pulled from the URLs listed. 'Verified' means those extracts matched SEED. I did not read any full text myself. Where something comes from my own memory, the item says so.

RESULT: no reference is fabricated or wrong. Every volume and start page SEED gives matches.
- The Albayrak & Vachaspati 2026 preprint (arXiv:2603.10115) exists. Its title, authors (Omer Albayrak and Tanmay Vachaspati, ASU) and submission date (10 March 2026) are confirmed. It is about global vortices in 2+1 dimensions, produced through a quantum mediator field. Production is 'highly fractured on the A–v space' (A is packet amplitude, v is speed), with 'holes' and isolated regions.
- Albayrak & Vachaspati, PRD 109, 036001 and arXiv:2308.01962 are both confirmed.
- Mimura 1967 is J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 6(2), 131–176. The values π4(G2)=π5(G2)=0 are confirmed by a 2025 arXiv paper that credits them to Mimura and Toda.
- Luhn, Nasri & Ramond JMP 48, 123519: the abstract says A5 (a subgroup of SO(3), so real triplets) and PSL2(7) (a subgroup of SU(3)) are the two finite simple groups with such representations.
- The ATLAS L2(7) page refers to 'ATLAS of Finite Groups, page 3'. The GAP character table library lists the maximal subgroups as S4, S4 and 7:3.
- Gillard & Gresnigt: EPJC 79 and the DOI are confirmed.

MINOR CORRECTIONS:
1. Albayrak & Vachaspati 'Creating kinks with quantum mediation' was published 1 February 2024. The journal year is 2024; 2023 is only the preprint year.
2. Sutcliffe 2007 should carry the full reference Proc. R. Soc. A 463, 3001–3020, arXiv:0705.1468. Its Q=7 trefoil claim is confirmed. The proof that the 3/4 power is optimal is the upper bound E ≤ C|Q|^{3/4} of Lin & Yang (2004), Commun. Math. Phys. 249, 273, not Sutcliffe. Sutcliffe's computed energies agree with Ward's conjectured bound, which scales as Q^{3/4}.
3. DESI DR2 Results II is now also published as PRD 112, 083515 (2025), DOI 10.1103/tr6y-kpc6. The 3.1σ and 2.8/3.8/4.2σ figures are correct. A later DES-Dovekie recalibration lowers the 4.2σ figure to about 3.2σ.
4. Vakulenko & Kapitanskii: the Russian original is Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 246, 840–842. Some papers cite the translation as page 432 instead of 433.
5. The ATLAS publisher is Clarendon Press, Oxford, which is an imprint of Oxford University Press.

CAVEATS ON HOW SEED USES ITS SOURCES:
- §5 cites Weinberg 1964 for 'turns out to be GR'. That 1964 paper derives charge conservation and the equality of gravitational and inertial mass from the S-matrix. The derivation of Einstein's equations is in Weinberg 1965 (PR 138, B988) and in Deser 1970.
- §2 says Finkelstein & Rubinstein treat textbook spinor fields as 'point-limit stand-ins' for kinks. The abstract extracts I saw did not show this. It may be in the full text but is unconfirmed.
- In §4, the A&V 2026 detail 'gaps even at high energy' was not seen explicitly. Only 'holes' and fractured production across amplitude and speed were.
- The 'no Wess–Zumino term for G2' argument really depends on H^5(G2)=0, not only on π5=0. Both hold, but this is my own reasoning, not from a source.

items.item: §9: "Breit & Wheeler (1934). Collision of two light quanta. Phys. Rev. 46, 1087." (used in §2: two photons -> e+e-)
items.correct_details: G. Breit & J. A. Wheeler, "Collision of Two Light Quanta", Phys. Rev. 46, 1087 (1934), DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.46.1087.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: several reference lists give 'G. Breit, J.A. Wheeler, Phys. Rev. 46, 1087 (1934). DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.46.1087'. The first page shows it was received 23 Oct 1934 and computes e+e- pair production from two colliding light quanta, applied to cosmic-ray photons. The end page was not seen; it is 1087–1091 from my memory only. Direct DOI and APS access were blocked.

items.item: §9: "Skyrme (1961). A nonlinear field theory. Proc. R. Soc. A 260, 127."
items.correct_details: T. H. R. Skyrme, "A non-linear field theory", Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 260, 127–138 (1961), DOI 10.1098/rspa.1961.0018.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: INSPIRE gives Proc.Roy.Soc.Lond.A 260 (1961) 127-138. Aitchison's history paper (arXiv:2001.09944) cites 'A non-linear field theory, Proc. Roy. Soc. A 260, 127-138 (1961)'. A Wikipedia-derived record gives DOI 10.1098/rspa.1961.0018, bibcode 1961RSPSA.260..127S.

items.item: §9: "Derrick (1964). Why static solitons need something extra. J. Math. Phys. 5, 1252." (§4: no static fold from gradient energy alone)
items.correct_details: G. H. Derrick, "Comments on Nonlinear Wave Equations as Models for Elementary Particles", J. Math. Phys. 5, 1252–1254 (1964), DOI 10.1063/1.1704233.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the abstract says 'for a wide class of nonlinear wave equations there exist no stable time-independent solutions of finite energy'. It also considers time-periodic, localized solutions. The citation details came from INSPIRE and a citedrive record (DOI 10.1063/1.1704233). This supports SEED's gist (the origin of Derrick's theorem).

items.item: §9: "Weinberg (1964). Massless spin-2 couples universally. Phys. Rev. 135, B1049." (§5: 'A massless spin-2 field coupled consistently to all energy turns out to be general relativity (Weinberg 1964; Deser 1970)')
items.correct_details: S. Weinberg, "Photons and Gravitons in S-Matrix Theory: Derivation of Charge Conservation and Equality of Gravitational and Inertial Mass", Phys. Rev. 135, B1049–B1056 (1964), DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.135.B1049. Nuance: the 1964 paper proves universal coupling (gravitational mass equals inertial mass). The step 'it is GR' is closer to Weinberg, Phys. Rev. 138, B988 (1965), 'Photons and Gravitons in Perturbation Theory: Derivation of Maxwell's and Einstein's Equations', and to Deser 1970.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the APS record gives DOI 10.1103/PhysRev.135.B1049, received 13 Apr 1964, issue of 24 Aug 1964. It derives charge conservation and the equality of gravitational and inertial mass from Lorentz invariance, pole structure and massless spin-1/spin-2 particles. The follow-up PR 138, B988 (1965) derives Maxwell's and Einstein's equations.

items.item: §9: "Mimura (1967). The homotopy groups of Lie groups of low rank (π₄(G₂) = π₅(G₂) = 0). J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 6, 131." (§2: G2 has no FR loop and no WZ term)
items.correct_details: M. Mimura, "The homotopy groups of Lie groups of low rank", J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 6(2), 131–176 (1967), DOI 10.1215/kjm/1250524375. π3(G2)=Z, π4(G2)=0, π5(G2)=0, π6(G2)=Z3.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: Project Euclid lists 'J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 6-2 (1967) 131-176'. The paper aims to determine the first 23 homotopy groups of low-rank groups, using G2/SU(3)=S^6. A 2025 arXiv paper on G2 gauge groups (arXiv:2512.12195) credits the low-degree values to Mimura and Toda and lists π4(G2)=0 and π5(G2)=0. Another note confirms π6(G2)≅Z/3 'as established in Mimura's classical calculations'. I did not see Mimura's own table directly. Separately, and as my own reasoning rather than a source: the absence of a WZ term really depends on H^5(G2;R)=0 (G2's real cohomology is generated in degrees 3 and 11). That is consistent with SEED's conclusion.

items.item: §9: "Finkelstein & Rubinstein (1968). Connection between spin, statistics, and kinks. J. Math. Phys. 9, 1762." (§2: FR proposed the reading 'with the spinor fields of textbooks as point-limit stand-ins for kinks of a nonlinear field')
items.correct_details: David Finkelstein & Julio Rubinstein, "Connection between Spin, Statistics, and Kinks", J. Math. Phys. 9(11), 1762–1779 (1968), DOI 10.1063/1.1664510.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the AIP abstract page and OSTI: sufficiently nonlinear classical fields have kinks conserved by boundary conditions and continuity. A rotating kink can have half-odd angular momentum if double-valued state functionals are allowed. For integer intrinsic angular momentum, the usual spin–statistics relation follows from continuity, with parastatistics excluded. The 'spinor fields as point-limit stand-ins' wording SEED attributes to FR did not appear in the extracts. It may be in the full text but is unverified.

items.item: §9: "Deser (1970). Self-interaction and gauge invariance. Gen. Rel. Grav. 1, 9."
items.correct_details: S. Deser, "Self-Interaction and Gauge Invariance", Gen. Rel. Grav. 1, 9–18 (1970), DOI 10.1007/BF00759198 (DOI from my memory, not seen). Reprint: arXiv:gr-qc/0411023.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the arXiv record: journal reference Gen.Rel.Grav.1:9-18,1970, received 17 Oct 1969 (Brandeis/Nordita). The abstract gives a closed-form derivation of the nonlinear terms of Einstein gravity and Yang–Mills from the conserved currents of the linear gauge invariance. This supports SEED's §5 use.

items.item: §9: "Günaydin & Gürsey (1973). Quark structure and octonions. J. Math. Phys. 14, 1651." (§3: SU(3) ⊂ G2 as the subgroup fixing one imaginary octonion)
items.correct_details: M. Günaydin & F. Gürsey, "Quark structure and octonions", J. Math. Phys. 14, 1651–1667 (1973), DOI 10.1063/1.1666240 (DOI from my memory, not seen).
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the Penn State record: 'The octonion (Cayley) algebra is studied in a split basis by means of a formalism that brings out its quark structure... the physically important subgroups SU(3) and SU(2)×SU(2) of G2, the automorphism group of octonions'. Secondary sources (e.g. arXiv:2609.10569, 1806.00612) describe SU(3) as the G2 stabilizer of an imaginary unit, with octonions splitting as 1+3+3̄+1.

items.item: §9: "Vakulenko & Kapitanskii (1979). The Hopf-charge energy bound. Sov. Phys. Dokl. 24, 433." (§4: E ≥ c|Q|^{3/4})
items.correct_details: A. F. Vakulenko & L. V. Kapitanskii, "Stability of solitons in S² in the nonlinear σ-model", Dokl. Akad. Nauk SSSR 246(4), 840–842 (1979), presented by Faddeev, received 2 Jan 1979. English translation: Sov. Phys. Dokl. 24, 433 (1979); a minority of citing papers give p. 432. The bound is E ≥ c|Q|^{3/4}.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the Math-Net.ru record gives the Doklady original (vol. 246, no. 4, pp. 840–842). Citing papers (arXiv:1904.00250, hep-th/0108047) give 'Sov. Phys. Dokl. 24, 433 (1979)', while arXiv:1404.4867 gives 432. The review arXiv:0804.1357 gives E ≥ c|Q|^{3/4} with c=(3/16)^{3/8}, attributed to V&K. SEED's citation is fine; the only correction is to add the original Doklady reference and note the 432/433 discrepancy.

items.item: §9: "Weinberg & Witten (1980). Limits on which massless particles can be composite. Phys. Lett. B 96, 59." (§8)
items.correct_details: S. Weinberg & E. Witten, "Limits on massless particles", Phys. Lett. B 96(1-2), 59–62 (1980), DOI 10.1016/0370-2693(80)90212-9 (DOI from my memory, not seen).
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the Princeton record: with a Lorentz-covariant energy-momentum tensor, 'composite as well as elementary massless particles with j > 1 are forbidden'. With a Lorentz-covariant conserved current, no massless particles carrying that charge with j > 1/2. This supports SEED's §8 use.

items.item: §9: "Witten (1983). ... Nucl. Phys. B 223, 422" (the Wess–Zumino term)
items.correct_details: E. Witten, "Global aspects of current algebra", Nucl. Phys. B 223, 422–432 (1983).
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the Princeton record and INSPIRE: pages 422–432. The abstract sets out the mathematical framework of the Wess–Zumino chiral action, which obeys a quantization law analogous to Dirac's for magnetic charge.

items.item: §9: "Witten (1983). Skyrmions from QCD ... Nucl. Phys. B 223, ... 433" (§2: the fold is a fermion when N_c is odd)
items.correct_details: E. Witten, "Current algebra, baryons, and quark confinement", Nucl. Phys. B 223, 433–444 (1983).
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the abstract (ScienceDirect/OSTI) and the full-text PDF copy: the abstract says 'ordinary baryons can be understood as solitons in current algebra effective lagrangians'. The text says a 2π rotation gives a phase (−1)^N: 'for odd N the soliton is a fermion; for even N it is a boson.' This supports SEED's §2 claim.

items.item: §9: "Adkins, Nappi & Witten (1983). Static properties of nucleons in the Skyrme model. Nucl. Phys. B 228, 552." (§6: nucleons within roughly 30%)
items.correct_details: G. S. Adkins, C. R. Nappi & E. Witten, "Static properties of nucleons in the Skyrme model", Nucl. Phys. B 228(3), 552–566 (1983).
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the Princeton record: pages 552–566, Dec 1983. Per the search summary, the abstract states the results are generally within about 30% of experimental values. This supports SEED's 'roughly 30%'.

items.item: §9: "Guadagnini (1984). Baryons as solitons and mass formulae. Nucl. Phys. B 236, 35." (§6: octet and decuplet from the SU(3) Skyrme model, mass formulae)
items.correct_details: E. Guadagnini, "Baryons as solitons and mass formulae", Nucl. Phys. B 236, 35 (1984). The end page, 47, is from my memory and was not seen.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the Pisa repository record: 'the Wess-Zumino term gives the right quantum numbers for the baryons, which appear as solitons in current algebra lagrangians. In the models, the mass formulae for the baryons are derived.' Reference lists (arXiv:hep-ph/0404173, hep-ph/0408121) cite 'Nucl. Phys. B 236 (1984) 35'; one Springer reference list has a 'B238' typo. A related SU(3) Skyrme paper notes that the WZ constraint makes the lowest multiplets the J=1/2 octet and J=3/2 decuplet.

items.item: §9: "Conway, Curtis, Norton, Parker & Wilson (1985). ATLAS of Finite Groups. Oxford University Press. L₂(7) on p. 3: maximal subgroups S₄, S₄ and 7:3." (§3: order-21 group is maximal in PSL(2,7))
items.correct_details: J. H. Conway, R. T. Curtis, S. P. Norton, R. A. Parker, R. A. Wilson, ATLAS of Finite Groups: Maximal Subgroups and Ordinary Characters for Simple Groups, Clarendon Press (Oxford University Press), Oxford, 1985, ISBN 0-19-853199-0. L2(7) ≅ L3(2) is on p. 3. Maximal subgroups: S4 (index 7), a second S4 class (index 7), and 7:3 (order 21, index 8).
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the QMUL online ATLAS page for L2(7) says 'Order = 168 ... See also the ATLAS of Finite Groups, page 3.' The GAP Character Table Library for L3(2) lists the maximal subgroups as S4 (24, index 7), S4 (24, index 7), 7:3 (21, index 8). Leemans' subgroup-lattice atlas agrees. The CiNii catalogue confirms Clarendon Press, Oxford, 1985, ISBN 0198531990. I did not see page 3 of the printed book itself.

items.item: §9: "Faddeev & Niemi (1997). Stable knot-like structures in classical field theory. Nature 387, 58."
items.correct_details: L. Faddeev & A. J. Niemi, "Stable knot-like structures in classical field theory", Nature 387, 58–61 (1997), DOI 10.1038/387058a0. The arXiv version is titled "Knots and Particles", hep-th/9610193.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the Nature listing gives Nature 387, 58–61, DOI 10.1038/387058a0. The arXiv record hep-th/9610193 ('Knots and Particles', submitted 24 Oct 1996) has journal reference Nature 387:58 (1997). Note that Battye & Sutcliffe 1998 later found most of FN's structural claims incorrect.

items.item: §9: "Battye & Sutcliffe (1998). Knots as stable soliton solutions. Phys. Rev. Lett. 81, 4798." (§4: at Q = 7 the minimum is a trefoil)
items.correct_details: R. A. Battye & P. M. Sutcliffe, "Knots as Stable Soliton Solutions in a Three-Dimensional Classical Field Theory", Phys. Rev. Lett. 81, 4798–4801 (1998). The arXiv version is titled "To be or knot to be?", hep-th/9808129.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the arXiv record has journal reference Phys.Rev.Lett.81:4798-4801,1998. The abstract covers minimum-energy configurations for charges 1–8: closed loops, linked loops and knots. Reviews say this work found 'the first non-trivial knot—the trefoil knot—for N=7'. This supports SEED's Q=7 trefoil claim.

items.item: §9: "Manton & Sutcliffe (2004). Topological Solitons. Cambridge University Press. The textbook."
items.correct_details: N. Manton & P. Sutcliffe, Topological Solitons, Cambridge Monographs on Mathematical Physics, Cambridge University Press, 2004, xi+493 pp., ISBN 978-0-521-83836-8.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: library catalogues give Cambridge University Press, 2004, xi, 493 p., ISBN 9780521838368 (0521838363), Cambridge Monographs on Mathematical Physics.

items.item: §9: "Luhn, Nasri & Ramond (2007). Simple finite non-Abelian flavor groups (PSL(2,7) inside SU(3)). J. Math. Phys. 48, 123519." (§3: PSL(2,7) is the only simple subgroup of SU(3) with a complex 3-dim irrep; the other, A5, has real triplets)
items.correct_details: C. Luhn, S. Nasri & P. Ramond, "Simple Finite Non-Abelian Flavor Groups", J. Math. Phys. 48, 123519 (2007), DOI 10.1063/1.2823978, arXiv:0709.1447.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the INIS record and abstract: the paper 'details the mathematics of the two finite simple groups with such [two- and three-dimensional irreducible] representations, the icosahedral group A5, a subgroup of SO(3), and PSL2(7), a subgroup of SU(3)'. A5 lying in SO(3) means its triplets are real; PSL(2,7) has one complex 3-dim irrep and its conjugate (from a related source). SEED's 'complex vs real triplet' phrasing is its own paraphrase but is consistent with, and implied by, the abstract. I did not read the body text.

items.item: §9: "[Luhn, Nasri & Ramond 2007] Also ℤ₇⋊ℤ₃ as a family symmetry, Phys. Lett. B 652, 27."
items.correct_details: C. Luhn, S. Nasri & P. Ramond, "Tri-Bimaximal Neutrino Mixing and the Family Symmetry Z7 ⋊ Z3", Phys. Lett. B 652, 27–33 (2007), arXiv:0706.2341.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the arXiv listing: journal reference Phys. Lett. B 652, 27–33 (2007), submitted June 2007 and revised Sept 2007. It studies the 21-element Frobenius group Z7⋊Z3 as a family symmetry that gives tri-bimaximal mixing. This supports SEED's 'flavor model-builders have used both groups'.

items.item: §9: "Sutcliffe (2007). Knots in the Skyrme–Faddeev model (the 3/4 power is optimal; Q = 7 is a trefoil). Proc. R. Soc. A, doi:10.1098/rspa.2007.0038." (§4)
items.correct_details: P. Sutcliffe, "Knots in the Skyrme–Faddeev model", Proc. R. Soc. A 463, 3001–3020 (2007), doi:10.1098/rspa.2007.0038, arXiv:0705.1468. The Q=7 trefoil claim is supported. The optimality of the 3/4 power comes from the upper bound E ≤ C|Q|^{3/4} of F. Lin & Y. Yang, 'Existence of energy minimizers as stable knotted solitons in the Faddeev model', Commun. Math. Phys. 249, 273 (2004). Combined with Vakulenko–Kapitanskii's lower bound, that makes 3/4 optimal, so that work should be cited for the optimality claim. Sutcliffe's own result is that the computed energies agree with Ward's conjectured bound.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the arXiv/ADS record gives Proc.Roy.Soc.Lond.A463:3001-3020,2007 and DOI 10.1098/rspa.2007.0038. The abstract covers simulations up to Hopf charge 16, with torus knots that are often only local minima and links as the global minima, and says 'the computed energies are in agreement with Ward's conjectured energy bound'. The text says 'the minimal energy soliton with Hopf charge seven is a trefoil knot'. The Lin–Yang abstract (Springer 10.1360/02ys0351) gives E ≤ C|Q|^{3/4}. I did not see whether Sutcliffe's paper itself states that the exponent is optimal.

items.item: §9: "Dutta, Steer & Vachaspati (2008). Creating kinks from particles. Phys. Rev. Lett. 101, 121601." (§4/§6: trains of small pulses make kink–antikink pairs over a wide range, most easily at low speed)
items.correct_details: S. Dutta, D. A. Steer & T. Vachaspati, "Creating Kinks from Particles", Phys. Rev. Lett. 101, 121601 (2008), DOI 10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.121601, arXiv:0803.0670.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the APS abstract page: 'We study the creation of solitons from particles, using the λφ⁴ model as a prototype'. They scatter trains of small identical wave pulses, and kink–antikink pairs are produced over a wide range of parameter space. 'Scattering at low velocities is favorable for creating solitons that have large energy compared to the mass of a particle.' Received 10 Mar 2008, published 16 Sep 2008. This supports SEED's uses.

items.item: §9: "Gillard & Gresnigt (2019). Three fermion generations with two unbroken gauge symmetries from the complex sedenions. Eur. Phys. J. C 79, doi:10.1140/epjc/s10052-019-6967-1."
items.correct_details: A. B. Gillard & N. G. Gresnigt, "Three fermion generations with two unbroken gauge symmetries from the complex sedenions", Eur. Phys. J. C 79(5), 446 (2019), DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-019-6967-1, arXiv:1904.03186. The article number 446 is from my memory; the sources I reached did not show it. SEED gives no article number.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the SCOAP3 and DOAJ records: EPJC vol. 79, issue 5 (May 2019), DOI 10.1140/epjc/s10052-019-6967-1, arXiv:1904.03186. The abstract says complexified sedenions describe three generations of leptons and quarks with unbroken SU(3)c×U(1)em, via a primitive idempotent that splits the algebra into three complex-octonion subalgebras sharing a quaternionic subalgebra. SEED does not use this reference elsewhere in the body.

items.item: §9: "STAR Collaboration (2021). Breit–Wheeler pairs from photon collisions. Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 052302." (§2: measured at RHIC in 2021 using photons around passing gold nuclei)
items.correct_details: STAR Collaboration (J. Adam et al.), "Measurement of e+e− Momentum and Angular Distributions from Linearly Polarized Photon Collisions", Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 052302 (2021), arXiv:1910.12400. The author name 'J. Adam et al.' is from my memory.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the institutional records and the arXiv abstract: 6085 exclusive e+e− pairs in ultraperipheral Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV; cos4Δφ modulation (16.8±2.5)%; 'consistent with QED calculations for the collision of linearly polarized photons quantized from the extremely strong electromagnetic fields generated by the highly charged Au nuclei'. Published July 2021. The title does not say 'Breit–Wheeler', but STAR and the press framed it that way. Caveat: the photons are quasi-real, so calling it a pure Breit–Wheeler measurement is debated.

items.item: §9: "Albayrak & Vachaspati (2023). Creating kinks with quantum mediation (Gaussian packets of a second field). Phys. Rev. D 109, 036001; arXiv:2308.01962." (§4: wide, energetic, slow packets work best; without the go-between no kinks form)
items.correct_details: O. Albayrak & T. Vachaspati, "Creating kinks with quantum mediation", Phys. Rev. D 109, 036001, published 1 February 2024, DOI 10.1103/PhysRevD.109.036001, arXiv:2308.01962 (v1 August 2023, v2 February 2024). The journal year is 2024; 2023 is only the preprint year.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the arXiv record, the APS abstract and the INIS record ('Published February 1, 2024'): kink–antikink pairs of φ are created by scattering classical wavepackets of ψ, 'only due to a quantum field that interacts with both φ and ψ'. 'Kink production is favored when the initial wavepackets have large total energy and wide spatial extent but scatter at low velocities.' The volume, article number and arXiv id all match SEED. This supports SEED's §4 description.

items.item: §9: "DESI Collaboration (2025). DR2 Results II: BAO measurements and cosmological constraints. arXiv:2503.14738." (§5: 3.1σ from BAO+CMB; 2.8–4.2σ with supernovae)
items.correct_details: DESI Collaboration (M. Abdul-Karim et al.), "DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints", arXiv:2503.14738 (v1 18 Mar 2025, v3 9 Oct 2025). Published as Phys. Rev. D 112, 083515 (2025), DOI 10.1103/tr6y-kpc6. SEED's arXiv id is correct; the published journal reference could be added. The w0waCDM preference over ΛCDM is 3.1σ (DESI+CMB) and 2.8σ / 3.8σ / 4.2σ with Pantheon+ / Union3 / DES-SN5YR.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts: the arXiv record and OSTI (ID 3011041) give PRD 112(8), 083515 and DOI 10.1103/tr6y-kpc6. The abstract mentions a 2.3σ BAO–CMB tension in ΛCDM, eased by evolving dark energy with w0>−1, wa<0. Secondary papers quoting DESI DR2: DESI BAO+CMB exclude ΛCDM at 3.1σ, and adding Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-SN5YR gives 2.8σ, 3.8σ and 4.2σ. So SEED's numbers are right. Later development: the DES-Dovekie recalibration lowers the DESY5 figure to about 3.2σ (arXiv:2508.10514), which further supports SEED's 'not yet decisive'.

items.item: §9: "Albayrak & Vachaspati (2026). Production of global vortices with quantum mediation. arXiv:2603.10115." (§4: 2D follow-up makes vortices, no sharp threshold, production fractured across packet height and speed, gaps even at high energy)
items.correct_details: Omer Albayrak & Tanmay Vachaspati (Arizona State Univ.), "Production of global vortices with quantum mediation", arXiv:2603.10115 [hep-ph, cross-listed hep-th], submitted 10 March 2026. No journal reference was seen.
items.evidence: From WebSearch extracts of the arXiv abstract and HTML v1: the setup is in 2+1 dimensions, with a complex scalar field carrying global vortices, a real scalar scatterer, and a quantum mediator coupling the two. Relativistic Gaussian wavepackets collide with speed v. 'Vortex production is highly sensitive to the initial Gaussian parameters, and the parameter space is chaotic with "holes" and isolated regions of vortex production.' The amplitude A versus velocity v scans at several widths show 'production is highly fractured on the A-v space'. It builds on arXiv:2308.01962. This supports SEED's description (height = amplitude A, speed = v). The specific phrase 'gaps even at high energy' was not seen verbatim; 'holes' was.

claims.summary:
Access caveat: I could not open any page directly. WebFetch failed with DNS errors (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) on every host I tried: arxiv.org, inspirehep.net, en.wikipedia.org. curl through the agent proxy got 403 CONNECT denials from arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, ar5iv, inspirehep.net, ui.adsabs.harvard.edu, journals.aps.org, doi.org, pdg.lbl.gov, wikipedia, osti, springer, aip, projecteuclid, desi.lbl.gov and others. Only github.com was reachable. All evidence below therefore comes from WebSearch result excerpts (search-engine text taken from abstract pages and secondary sources), from standard homotopy-theory derivations I worked through myself (marked as derivations), and from CODATA constants computed locally with scipy 1.18.1 (CODATA 2022). No full text was read. For each item, the source_url is the page whose search excerpt I saw; none of these pages was opened.

Bottom line: most claims in sections 2, 4, 5 and 8 hold up.
- All the topology claims check out: pi4(SU(2))=Z2, pi4(S^2)=Z2, pi4(SU(3))=0, pi4(G2)=pi5(G2)=0, pi3(G)=Z, pi3(S^2)=Z, pi2(SU(3)/T^2)=Z^2, pi3(SU(3)/T^2)=Z.
- The Finkelstein-Rubinstein abstract really does contain the 'point-limit' spinor reading.
- Auckly and Speight independently support the claim that a G2 Skyrme field gives only bosonic folds.
- The DESI numbers are exact: 3.1 sigma for DESI+CMB, and 2.8 / 3.8 / 4.2 sigma with Pantheon+ / Union3 / DES-SN5YR. A later DES-Dovekie recalibration lowers the DES figure to about 3.2 sigma.
- The proton and electron length scales are correct.

Corrections needed:
1. Section 4: the proof that the 3/4 power is the right one is Lin & Yang 2004 (Commun. Math. Phys. 249, 273), not Sutcliffe 2007. Sutcliffe's numerics agree with Ward's conjectured ~Q^{3/4} bound.
2. Section 5: Weinberg 1964 derives universal coupling (gravitational mass equals inertial mass). The derivation of Einstein's equations is Weinberg 1965, Phys. Rev. 138, B988.
3. Section 8: the electron size bound is conservative. LEP gives r_e < 1.1e-19 m = 1.1e-4 fm, so the Compton-wavelength mismatch is at least about 3.5e6. 'At least 1e5' is still true.
4. Weinberg-Witten blocks charged massless |h|>1/2 states (under a Lorentz-covariant conserved current) and |h|>1 states (with a Lorentz-covariant conserved T_mu_nu). It forbids composite gravitons in such theories, but not a neutral composite photon.
5. STAR 2021 is real, but the photons are quasi-real, whether this counts as Breit-Wheeler is debated, and it was not the first observation of gamma-gamma to e+e- in heavy-ion collisions.

Could not confirm:
- The detailed Dutta-Steer-Vachaspati parameters (number of pulses, amplitudes, speeds).
- The specifics of the 2026 vortex paper beyond its abstract: that the scanned axes were packet height and speed, and the 'gaps even at high energy' wording. The abstract does say production is 'chaotic with holes and isolated regions'.

Bibliography notes, for the other agent:
- Dutta's first name is Sourish.
- Albayrak & Vachaspati PRD 109, 036001 was published in 2024; the arXiv version is from 2023.
- The DESI DR2 II PRD article number appears as both 112, 083514 and 083515 in different listings.

items.item: §2: 'For SU(2) ... turning a fold once around traces a loop that can't be shrunk away (π₄ = ℤ₂)'
items.correct_details: π4(SU(2)) = π4(S³) = Z2. For based Skyrme fields the configuration space Maps_*(S³,SU(2)) has π1 = π4(SU(2)) = Z2. The 2π-rotation loop is the non-contractible generator for odd baryon number, so for a single fold the statement is right.
items.evidence: Derivation: SU(2)≅S³, and π4(S³)=Z2 is classical (Freudenthal). Search excerpts: hep-lat/9504007 says π4(SU(2))=Z2 underlies Witten's anomaly. arXiv:1710.04218 lists π4(SU(3))=0 alongside π4(SU(2))=Z2. hep-ph/0105255 ties the nontrivial π4(SU(2)) class to fermionic Skyrmion quantization. Pages not opened.

items.item: §2: '...and for the S² of the knot models ... (π₄ = ℤ₂)'
items.correct_details: π4(S²) ≅ π4(S³) = Z2 via the Hopf fibration. Maps_*(S³,S²) = Ω³S² is a loop space, so every charge sector has π1 = Z2. Nuance: Krusch & Speight (Commun. Math. Phys. 264, 391 (2006)) show Hopf solitons can be quantized as fermions when the Hopf charge Q is odd. The rotation loop is non-contractible only for odd Q, not for every fold.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt, Krusch & Speight abstract] 'Hopf solitons can be quantized as fermions if their Hopf charge is odd'; the loops are generated by symmetries of the minimal-energy configurations. [Search excerpt, Auckly & Speight hep-th/0411010] 'fermionic quantization of Hopfions is always possible.' Derivation of π4(S²) from the Hopf fibration long exact sequence.

items.item: §2: 'For SU(3) the loop does shrink (π₄ = 0)'
items.correct_details: π4(SU(3)) = 0 (and π5(SU(3)) = Z). SU(n) is in the Bott stable range for k ≤ 2n−1, and π4(SU) = 0, π5(SU) = Z.
items.evidence: Derivation: the fibration SU(3)→SU(4)→S⁷ gives π_k(SU(3)) ≅ π_k(SU) for k ≤ 5; Bott periodicity gives π_even(U)=0 and π_odd(U)=Z. [Search excerpt] arXiv:1710.04218 lists π4(SU(3))=0 and describes the sequence π5(SU(3))→π5(S⁵)→π4(SU(2))→0 with maps ×2 and mod 2.

items.item: §2: 'the Wess–Zumino term supplies the sign instead, and the fold is a fermion when the number of colors N_c is odd (Witten 1983)'
items.correct_details: Correct. Witten, 'Current algebra, baryons, and quark confinement', Nucl. Phys. B 223 (1983) 433–444: with the WZ term of coefficient N_c, the 2π rotation of the SU(3) skyrmion gives the phase (−1)^{N_c}, so the skyrmion is a fermion iff N_c is odd. The companion paper NPB 223, 422 ('Global aspects of current algebra') introduces the WZ term.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] The NPB 223 (1983) 433–444 abstract: 'ordinary baryons can be understood as solitons in current algebra effective lagrangians.' Secondary sources: Tong's gauge-theory notes say the WZ term 'makes the Skyrmion fermionic or bosonic depending on the number of colours N_c'; a review says 'for odd N colour, skyrmions actually have half-integer spin'. I did not see the primary abstract's own wording on N_c.

items.item: §2: 'Finkelstein and Rubinstein (1968) proposed this reading, with the spinor fields of textbooks as point-limit stand-ins for kinks of a nonlinear field'
items.correct_details: Correct. Finkelstein & Rubinstein, J. Math. Phys. 9, 1762–1779 (1968), DOI 10.1063/1.1664510.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt of the ADS/AIP abstract] 'Sufficiently nonlinear classical fields admit modes called kinks, whose number is strictly conserved...' 'even if the intrinsic angular momentum is an integer, a rotating kink can have half-odd angular momentum, if double-valued state functionals are admitted' ... 'for fields with integer-valued intrinsic angular momentum, the observed relation between spin and (exchange) statistics follows from continuity alone, parastatistics being excluded' ... 'consistent with the hypothesis that the spinor fields usually employed to describe half-odd-spin quanta are not fundamental, but are useful "point-limit" approximations to such operators.'

items.item: §2: 'For G₂ neither route exists: π₄ = π₅ = 0 (Mimura 1967)'
items.evidence: [Search excerpt] A recent paper on G2 gauge groups (arXiv:2607.03684 / 2512.06696) tabulates π4(G2)≅0, π5(G2)≅0, π6(G2)≅Z/3, attributed to Mimura. Ōshima: π_m(G2) is infinite only for m∈{3,11}, and ⟨π3,π3⟩=π6(G2)=Z3. Independent derivation: Spin(7)/G2 = S⁷ gives π_k(G2) ≅ π_k(Spin(7)) for k ≤ 5. SO(7) is stable for k ≤ 5, and Bott gives π4(SO)=π5(SO)=0, so π4(G2)=π5(G2)=0. Mimura's own text was not read.

items.item: §2: '...so there is no such loop and no Wess–Zumino term, and a G₂-valued field alone makes only bosonic folds'
items.correct_details: Correct. With π4(G2)=0, π1 of the Skyrme configuration space is trivial. H⁵(G2;R)=0 because the rational cohomology generators sit in degrees 3 and 11, so there is no WZ term. Auckly & Speight's general classification agrees.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt, Auckly & Speight, 'Fermionic quantization and configuration spaces for the Skyrme and Faddeev-Hopf models', hep-th/0411010, Commun. Math. Phys. 263 (2006) 173] 'Fermionic quantization of Skyrmions is possible only if the target group contains a symplectic or special unitary factor, while fermionic quantization of Hopfions is always possible.' G2 contains neither factor. The excerpt does not mention G2 by name; applying the result to G2 is my inference.

items.item: §2: 'two photons can become an electron and a positron (Breit–Wheeler, 1934)'
items.correct_details: G. Breit & J. A. Wheeler, 'Collision of Two Light Quanta', Phys. Rev. 46, 1087 (1934), received 23 Oct 1934, issue of 15 Dec 1934. The process is γγ→e⁺e⁻.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] Several sources give Phys. Rev. 46(12), 1087 (1934). The paper computes γγ→e⁺e⁻ cross sections and angular distributions for different polarizations and applies them to cosmic-ray photons on background radiation.

items.item: §2: 'It was measured at RHIC in 2021, using the photons that surround passing gold nuclei' (STAR, PRL 127, 052302)
items.correct_details: STAR Collaboration, 'Measurement of e⁺e⁻ Momentum and Angular Distributions from Linearly Polarized Photon Collisions', Phys. Rev. Lett. 127, 052302 (published 27 July 2021), arXiv:1910.12400. 6085 exclusive e⁺e⁻ pairs in ultra-peripheral Au+Au at √s_NN = 200 GeV, plus a peripheral-collision sample (centrality dependence). Caveats: the photons are quasi-real Weizsäcker–Williams photons of small virtuality; a later STAR paper (PRC 111, 014909) notes 'there is no clear consensus on what is considered as the Breit-Wheeler process in UPCs'. γγ→e⁺e⁻ in heavy-ion ultra-peripheral collisions had been studied before (e.g. STAR 2004), so 2021 was a differential measurement interpreted as Breit–Wheeler, not the first sighting.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt of the abstract] 'The Breit-Wheeler process which produces matter and anti-matter from photon collisions is investigated experimentally through the observation of 6085 exclusive electron-positron pairs in ultra-peripheral Au+Au collisions at √sNN = 200 GeV'; cos4Δφ modulation (16.8±2.5)%; √⟨P⊥²⟩ = 38.1±0.9 MeV; 'consistent with QED calculations for the collision of linearly polarized photons'.

items.item: §2: 'One speed. Every massless signal shares the cone: light, gravitational waves'
items.correct_details: This is a consequence of the framework, and it matches observation: GW170817/GRB 170817A bound −3×10⁻¹⁵ < (v_gw − c)/c < +7×10⁻¹⁶ (LIGO/Virgo/Fermi/INTEGRAL, ApJL 848, L13 (2017), arXiv:1710.05834).
items.evidence: [Search excerpt] 'the observed time delay of (+1.74±0.05)s between GRB 170817A and GW170817 constrains the difference between the speed of gravity and the speed of light to be between −3×10⁻¹⁵ and +7×10⁻¹⁶ times the speed of light.'

items.item: §2: 'No vacuum dispersion. Light of every energy crosses empty space at the same speed.'
items.correct_details: Consistent with data. Fermi GRB 090510 gives E_QG,1 > 1.2 E_Planck for linear energy dependence (Abdo et al., Nature 462, 331 (2009)). Later Fermi-LAT reanalysis (arXiv:1305.3463) gives up to 7.6 E_Planck (subluminal, linear, without intrinsic-dispersion modelling).
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] The Nature paper reports no evidence for Lorentz-invariance violation and a lower bound of 1.2 Planck energies on the linear scale. The 2013 reanalysis gives 7.6 E_Pl, or about 2 E_Pl when only the LIV-induced part is used.

items.item: §2: 'Equivalence principle. Everything falls the same way'
items.correct_details: Consistent with data. MICROSCOPE final: η(Ti,Pt) = [−1.5 ± 2.3(stat) ± 1.5(syst)]×10⁻¹⁵ (PRL 129, 121102 (2022), arXiv:2209.15487).
items.evidence: [Search excerpt] MICROSCOPE finds no WEP violation, with η(Ti,Pt) = [−1.5 ± 2.3 (stat) ± 1.5 (syst)] × 10⁻¹⁵, about 2.7×10⁻¹⁵ combined.

items.item: §4: 'point-like folds: π₃ of the internal space, which is ℤ for SU(3), for G₂ and for every simple compact Lie group'
items.correct_details: Correct. π3(G)≅Z for every compact connected simple Lie group (Bott 1954/56, via Morse theory). π2(G)=0 for every compact connected Lie group (Cartan). π3 is unchanged by passing to covers, so it holds for non-simply-connected forms too.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt] 'for any connected Lie group H, π2(H) vanishes. If, moreover, H is simple, then π3(H) ≅ ℤ'; Bott's 'On torsion in Lie groups' (PNAS 1954) gives π3(G)≅Z for simple G. The G2 case also follows from the derivation above (π3(G2) ≅ π3(Spin(7)) = Z).

items.item: §4: 'monopoles: π₂ of the vacuum space ... a theory that unifies the forces in one simple group always has them'
items.correct_details: Standard result: for simply connected simple G broken to H ⊃ U(1)_em, π2(G/H) ≅ π1(H) ⊇ Z, so GUT monopoles exist ('t Hooft–Polyakov; Preskill, Ann. Rev. Nucl. Part. Sci. 1984). Minor caveat: arXiv:1007.3832 argues that when Alice strings exist (some SU(5)/SO(10) breakings) the conserved monopole charge can become Z2. Monopoles still exist, but the charge group changes.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] TASI cosmology notes (astro-ph/0401547): breaking a simple G gives π2(G/H)=π1(H), so breaking to the SM yields monopoles. arXiv:1007.3832: 'π2(G/H) ≅ π1(H) ≅ Z' because H contains U(1), plus the Alice-string loophole.

items.item: §4: 'knots: the Hopf number, π₃(S²) = ℤ'
items.correct_details: π3(S²)=Z (Hopf 1931). It follows from the Hopf fibration S¹→S³→S², which gives π3(S²)≅π3(S³)=Z.
items.evidence: Derivation from the long exact sequence of the Hopf fibration. Standard: arXiv:1306.2364 describes Faddeev–Niemi knots as stabilized by the Hopf invariant.

items.item: §4/§6A: 'In φ⁴, colliding trains of small pulses of the field itself make kink–antikink pairs over a wide range of settings, most easily at low speed (Dutta, Steer & Vachaspati 2008)'
items.correct_details: Matches the abstract of S. Dutta, D. A. Steer & T. Vachaspati, 'Creating Kinks from Particles', PRL 101, 121601 (2008), arXiv:0803.0670 (v1 title 'From Particles to Kinks'). Nuance: the abstract says low velocity is 'favorable for creating solitons that have large energy compared to the mass of a particle'. 'Most easily at low speed' is a fair but slightly stronger paraphrase. The first author is Sourish Dutta.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt of the abstract] 'We study the creation of solitons from particles, using the λφ⁴ model as a prototype. We consider the scattering of small, identical, wave pulses, which are equivalent to a sequence of particles, and find that kink-antikink pairs are created for a large region in parameter space. We also find that scattering at low velocities is favorable for creating solitons that have large energy compared to the mass of a particle.' The v1 abstract: 'a large class of initial conditions ... consisting of small, identical, incoming wave pulses, that scatter classically and create a kink-antikink pair.'

items.item: §4/§6A: exact Dutta–Steer–Vachaspati setup (number of pulses, amplitudes, widths, speeds scanned)
items.correct_details: Not determinable without the full text. The abstract confirms only 'small, identical, wave pulses ... equivalent to a sequence of particles'. The paper motivates its approach by noting that time-reversing kink–antikink annihilation would need finely controlled radiation; this comes from a snippet that may mix in the 2023 paper. For calibration targets, read arXiv:0803.0670 directly.
items.evidence: Several searches returned no parameter values. WebFetch and curl to arxiv.org failed (DNS failure / proxy 403).

items.item: §4: 'collides Gaussian packets of a second field that reaches the kink field only through a quantum go-between; wide, energetic, slow packets work best, and without the go-between no kinks form (Albayrak & Vachaspati 2023)'
items.correct_details: Correct in substance. O. Albayrak & T. Vachaspati, 'Creating kinks with quantum mediation', arXiv:2308.01962 (Aug 2023), published Phys. Rev. D 109, 036001 (1 Feb 2024). Note that the journal year is 2024. One search excerpt also reports 'a lower energy threshold' for kink production in this paper.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts of the abstract] Kink–antikink pairs of one scalar field are created by scattering classical wavepackets of a second scalar field with no direct interaction; 'the creation is only possible due to a quantum field that interacts with both'; 'We scan parameter space and find it favorable for kink production when the initial wavepackets have large total energy and wide spatial extent but scatter at low velocities.'

items.item: §4: '...follow-up in two space dimensions, which makes vortices, finds no sharp threshold: production is fractured ... with gaps (Albayrak & Vachaspati 2026)' (gist)
items.correct_details: Gist confirmed. O. Albayrak & T. Vachaspati, 'Production of global vortices with quantum mediation', arXiv:2603.10115 (10 Mar 2026). The setup is 2+1D, with a complex scalar hosting global vortices, a real scalar scatterer and a quantum mediator; relativistic Gaussian wavepackets are scattered.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt of the abstract] 'vortex production is highly sensitive to the initial Gaussian parameters, and the parameter space is chaotic with "holes" and isolated regions of vortex production.'

items.item: §4: 2026 specifics: 'fractured across packet height and speed, with gaps even at high energy'
items.correct_details: The abstract refers only to 'initial Gaussian parameters' and to holes and isolated regions. It does not say the scanned axes were amplitude (height) and velocity, and does not say gaps persist at high energy. Check against the full text before using as a calibration target.
items.evidence: Two targeted searches returned only the abstract-level statement. The full text (arxiv.org/html/2603.10115) was unreachable.

items.item: §4: 'In three dimensions a static fold can't be held by gradient energy alone (Derrick 1964)'
items.correct_details: G. H. Derrick, 'Comments on nonlinear wave equations as models for elementary particles', J. Math. Phys. 5, 1252–1254 (1964). There are no stable static finite-energy solutions for a wide class of scalar field theories with the standard two-derivative kinetic term (scaling/virial argument: I_grad + 3 I_pot = 0 in 3D). Time-periodic solutions (Q-ball-like) were noted as an escape route.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt, INSPIRE abstract] 'It is shown that for a wide class of nonlinear wave equations there exist no stable time-independent solutions of finite energy.' Also: 'the possibility that elementary particles might be oscillating solutions'.

items.item: §4: 'E ≥ c|Q|^{3/4} (Vakulenko & Kapitanskii 1979)'
items.correct_details: Correct: the Vakulenko–Kapitanskii lower bound E ≥ c|Q|^{3/4} for the Faddeev–Skyrme model (Sov. Phys. Dokl. 24, 433 (1979)). The constant c is not sharp.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] 'In 1979 Vakulenko and Kapitanskii obtained ... lower limit ("VK bound") ... E ≥ c|Q|^{3/4}'. Hirayama et al. note the analytic constant is far from optimal. Primary text not seen.

items.item: §4: 'the 3/4 power is known to be the right one, and the computed minima agree (Sutcliffe 2007)'; §9: 'the 3/4 power is optimal'
items.correct_details: Lin & Yang, 'Existence of energy minimizers as stable knotted solitons in the Faddeev model', Commun. Math. Phys. 249, 273 (2004), proved the matching upper bound E ≤ C|Q|^{3/4}, so the exponent 3/4 is optimal. Sutcliffe 2007 (Proc. R. Soc. A 463, 3001–3020, arXiv:0705.1468) is numerical: solutions up to Q=16, with energies 'in agreement with Ward's conjectured energy bound' (∝Q^{3/4}). Credit the optimality to Lin & Yang 2004, and cite Sutcliffe 2007 for the numerical agreement.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] Lin & Yang 2004: 'E and Q satisfy the sublinear inequality E ≤ C|Q|^{3/4}'; later summaries describe a two-sided estimate C⁻¹|Q|^{3/4} ≤ E ≤ C|Q|^{3/4}. Sutcliffe 2007 abstract: 'soliton solutions for Hopf charges up to sixteen ... The computed energies are in agreement with Ward's conjectured energy bound.'

items.item: §4/§6C: 'at Q = 7 it is a trefoil (Battye & Sutcliffe 1998, confirmed by Sutcliffe 2007)'
items.correct_details: Correct. Battye & Sutcliffe, PRL 81, 4798 (1998), computed minima for Q=1–8, including the first knot, a trefoil at Q=7. Sutcliffe 2007 finds the Q=7 minimal-energy soliton is the trefoil K_{3,2} (links at Q=5,6 and Q=8). Caveats from Sutcliffe 2007: energy gaps between competing knots and links are often only about 1%, and for some Q the minimum is not unique.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] BS1998 abstract: 'minimum energy configurations for charges one to eight ... closed loops, linked loops and, most interestingly, knots'. A hopfion review: 'found the first non-trivial knot—the trefoil knot—for N=7'. A citation of Sutcliffe 2007: 'The Q=7 minimal energy soliton has this form [K_{3,2}]'; 'no trefoil knots with Q<7'.

items.item: §6B: 'For nucleons the model lands within roughly 30% (Adkins, Nappi & Witten 1983)'
items.correct_details: ANW, Nucl. Phys. B 228, 552–566 (1983): static properties 'generally within about 30%' of experiment. Caveats: the N and Δ masses were used as inputs to fix F_π and e (recalled: F_π ≈ 129 MeV versus about 186 MeV experimentally, e ≈ 5.45; not re-verified). g_A ≈ 0.61 is about half of experiment, which a later paper flags as the exception.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt, ScienceDirect/ADS abstract] results 'generally within about 30% of experimental values' in the SU(2)×SU(2) chiral (Skyrme) model. [Excerpt, He–Mobed–Khanna] the 30% agreement holds 'except for the axial charge g_A, which is about half of the experimental value'.

items.item: §6B: 'Quantize its rotations and the lowest states fill the octet (hexagon) and the decuplet (triangle) (Guadagnini 1984)'
items.correct_details: E. Guadagnini, 'Baryons as solitons and mass formulae', Nucl. Phys. B 236, 35–47 (1984). The WZ term enforces the right quantum numbers (hypercharge constraint Y_R = N_c/3), the lowest SU(3) collective states are the spin-½ octet and spin-3/2 decuplet, and the paper derives the octet–decuplet mass relation now called the Guadagnini formula. Mazur–Nowak–Praszałowicz (1984) did related work independently.
items.evidence: [Search excerpt, partial abstract] 'It is shown that the Wess-Zumino term gives the right quantum numbers for the baryons, which appear as solitons in current algebra lagrangians. In these models, the mass formulae for the baryons are derived.' Secondary: 'Guadagnini relation ... valid for the ground state octet and decuplet'; SU(3) collective quantization 'predicts the well-known 8 and 10 SU(3) multiplets'.

items.item: §5: 'A massless spin-2 field coupled consistently to all energy turns out to be general relativity (Weinberg 1964; Deser 1970)'
items.correct_details: Weinberg 1964 (Phys. Rev. 135, B1049, 'Photons and Gravitons in S-Matrix Theory: Derivation of Charge Conservation and Equality of Gravitational and Inertial Mass') proves universal soft-graviton coupling, i.e. the equivalence principle, not the full Einstein equations. The derivation of Einstein's equations is Weinberg 1965, Phys. Rev. 138, B988 ('Photons and Gravitons in Perturbation Theory: Derivation of Maxwell's and Einstein's Equations'). Deser 1970 (Gen. Rel. Grav. 1, 9; repost gr-qc/0411023) gives the closed-form self-consistent derivation; the first-order formalism makes it terminate at a cubic self-interaction. Earlier work: Gupta, Kraichnan, Feynman. The result is GR up to a cosmological constant and higher-derivative terms.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] Weinberg 1964 abstract: 'a purely S-matrix-theoretic proof of the conservation of charge ... and of the equality of gravitational and inertial mass'; assumptions are 'Lorentz invariance and pole structure of the S matrix, and the zero mass and spins 1 and 2'. Weinberg 1965: spin-1 and spin-2 potentials 'must inevitably satisfy Maxwell's and Einstein's equations'. Deser 1970: 'unified closed-form derivation of the nonlinear terms for Einstein gravity, Yang-Mills...'; 'first-order formalism leads uniformly to a simple cubic self-interaction'.

items.item: §5: 'a mass makes the vacuum act like a medium with index n ≈ 1 + 2GM/(rc²)'
items.correct_details: Correct in the weak field, in isotropic coordinates: n = 1 − 2Φ/c² = 1 + 2GM/(rc²). Fermat's principle with this n gives the full GR deflection 4GM/(bc²) and the Shapiro delay. The exact isotropic Schwarzschild index is n = (1+M/2r)³/(1−M/2r) (G=c=1).
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] Narayan & Bartelmann lectures (astro-ph/9606001): 'n = 1 − (2/c²)Φ = 1 + (2/c²)|Φ|'. GR course notes give the isotropic-coordinate index and the Shapiro delay Δt = (2GM/c³) ln(4ρ₁ρ₂/b²).

items.item: §5: 'DESI's 2025 data prefer a slow drift: 3.1σ from BAO and the CMB, and 2.8–4.2σ once supernovae are added, depending on the sample'
items.correct_details: Correct (DESI DR2 Results II, arXiv:2503.14738; Phys. Rev. D 112 (2025), listed as 083514 or 083515 depending on the source). w0waCDM is preferred over ΛCDM at 3.1σ for DESI BAO+CMB. With supernovae: 2.8σ (Pantheon+), 3.8σ (Union3), 4.2σ (DES-SN5YR). Update: after the DES-Dovekie recalibration of DES-SN5YR, the DES figure falls to about 3.2σ, and adding SH0ES lowers all three. 'Not yet decisive' remains accurate.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] Edinburgh record of the DR2 paper: 'preferred over ΛCDM at 3.1σ for the combination of DESI BAO and CMB'; 'ranges from 2.8−4.2σ depending on which SNe sample is used'. A follow-up paper: 'Including additional supernova data sets Pantheon+, Union3, and DES SN5YR yields exclusion significances of 2.8σ, 3.8σ, and 4.2σ, respectively.' Dovekie re-analysis: 'reduced to ... 3.2σ, compared to the earlier 4.2σ'.

items.item: §8: 'The proton is (charge radius 0.84 fm ...)'
items.correct_details: CODATA 2022 proton rms charge radius = 0.84075(64) fm (CODATA 2018: 0.8414(19) fm; PDG about 0.8409(4) fm, recalled).
items.evidence: Local computation: scipy 1.18.1 physical_constants['proton rms charge radius'] = 8.4075e-16 m ± 6.4e-19 m (CODATA 2022 table bundled in scipy). Not fetched from NIST or PDG directly (proxy 403).

items.item: §8: '... against 0.21 fm' (proton reduced Compton wavelength)
items.correct_details: ħ/(m_p c) = 0.210309 fm. Charge radius divided by reduced Compton wavelength ≈ 4.0.

items.item: §8: 'its Compton wavelength is 386 fm' (electron, ħ/mc)

items.item: §8: 'no size shows down to about 10⁻³ fm ... The electron misses by at least 10⁵'
items.correct_details: Conservative. The best direct bound comes from LEP2 Bhabha and contact-interaction fits. The final LEP electroweak paper (Schael et al., Phys. Rept. 532, 119 (2013), arXiv:1302.3415) gives r_e < 1.1×10⁻¹⁹ m = 1.1×10⁻⁴ fm, assuming electromagnetic-strength coupling; stronger couplings tighten it. An earlier analysis (Bourilkov, hep-ph/0002172) gives r_e < 2.8×10⁻¹⁹ m (95% CL). Bounds from electron g−2 are model-dependent: about 3×10⁻¹⁸ m with chirally protected (m²) scaling, about 2×10⁻²³ m with linear scaling. With the LEP bound, 386 fm / 1.1×10⁻⁴ fm ≈ 3.5×10⁶. 'At least 10⁵' is true; the gap is at least about 10⁶.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] LEP EW review: 'r_e < 1.1 · 10⁻¹⁹ m', converted from the contact-interaction scale Λ assuming electromagnetic-strength coupling. hep-ph/0002172: 'upper limit on the electron size of 2.8·10⁻¹⁹ m at 95% CL'; g−2 bounds 'r_e ~ 2·10⁻²³ m' (linear) or about 3×10⁻¹⁸ m (quadratic, chiral). Local arithmetic: ħc/Λ is 2×10⁻⁵ fm at Λ = 10 TeV.

items.item: §8: 'In weakly coupled theories, folding a few quanta into a pair is exponentially rare'
items.correct_details: Correct. Demidov & Levkov ('Soliton-antisoliton pair production in particle collisions', arXiv:1103.0013; I recall PRL 107, 071601 (2011) but did not confirm it) find the semiclassical pair-production probability exponentially suppressed, with the suppression staying nearly constant at high energy. The companion JHEP 2011 paper (arXiv:1103.2133) finds classical pair creation needs parametrically many (about 1/g²) particles, so few-particle production is exponentially suppressed.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts] 1103.0013: probability 'suppressed by an exponentially small factor' that stays nearly constant at high energies. 1103.2133: particle number is parametrically large where classical creation occurs, so few-particle soliton–antisoliton production is exponentially suppressed. 1509.07125: solitons are about 1/g² particles, so probabilities are exponentially suppressed at weak coupling.

items.item: §8: 'Can light and the cone themselves be built from the field? Weinberg and Witten (1980) map where that's hard.'
items.correct_details: Weinberg & Witten, 'Limits on massless particles', Phys. Lett. B 96, 59 (1980). A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot have massless particles of helicity |h| > 1/2 that carry nonzero charge under it. A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor cannot have massless particles with |h| > 1. So an emergent graviton is excluded in any Lorentz-covariant theory with such a T_μν; known evasions include gauge-variant T (GR itself) and holography, where the graviton lives in a different spacetime. A neutral composite photon is NOT excluded by WW. 'Hard' fits gravity much better than light.
items.evidence: [Search excerpts of secondary sources] 'A theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot contain massless particles with helicity above 1/2 that carry a nonzero charge'; 'A Lorentz-covariant energy-momentum tensor rules out massless particles of helicity above 1'; citation Phys. Lett. B 96 (1980) 59. The original paper was not seen.

items.item: §7 (requested): flag space SU(3)/T²: 'π₂ = ℤ²' and 'π₃ = ℤ'
items.correct_details: Both correct. The moment-map image of the full flag (regular coadjoint orbit) is the convex hull of a Weyl orbit, a hexagon with 120° angles (generally alternating side lengths); this is the Kostant / Atiyah–Guillemin–Sternberg convexity theorem, recalled and not checked in a source.
items.evidence: Derivation, long exact sequence of T²→SU(3)→SU(3)/T²: π2(SU(3))=0 → π2(F) → π1(T²)=Z² → π1(SU(3))=0, so π2(F)=Z². π3(T²)=0 → π3(SU(3))=Z → π3(F) → π2(T²)=0, so π3(F)=Z. [Search excerpt] arXiv:2103.05035 notes the flag sigma model has two independent skyrmion charges, consistent with Z²; arXiv:1805.10008 builds Hopfions on F₂ = SU(3)/U(1)².

targets.quantity: Dutta-Steer-Vachaspati 2008 setup and region of kink production
targets.value: Model: lambda phi^4 in 1+1D. Two trains of N_b identical small breather-like pulses (no exact phi4 breathers exist), one from each side, with frequency omega near 1 (likely in meson-mass units; unconfirmed) and velocity v. Kink-antikink pairs form 'for a large region in parameter space'. Low velocities favor creating solitons with large energy compared to the particle mass. A search snippet attributes an example 'breather trains at omega = 0.99, v = 0.43 produce kinks' (attribution uncertain). Exact initial-condition formula, N_b, spacing, grid and phase-diagram boundaries: UNVERIFIABLE
targets.source: Dutta, Steer & Vachaspati, PRL 101, 121601 (2008), arXiv:0803.0670 (arXiv title 'From particles to kinks'; v3 dated 25 Aug 2008)
targets.notes: Abstract-level facts are confirmed by several search summaries. Related, but a different model (deformed O(3)/sine-Gordon): Vachaspati, PRD 84, 125003 (2011), arXiv:1109.1065, used N=4, omega=0.95, x0=32, a=11.1, w=5.55 and scanned v in [0.4, 0.95]. Its x_j = x0 + (j-1) a train layout is probably the same as DSV's (inference).

targets.quantity: Romanczukiewicz & Shnir 2010: kinks from colliding particle-like perturbations via oscillon resonance
targets.value: Three-stage mechanism: the collision forms an oscillon; incoming perturbations excite it resonantly; it decays into a kink-antikink pair (parametric resonance). Outcome depends fractally on perturbation amplitude, number of perturbations and wave number. A collective-coordinate model is given. Numerical parameters: UNVERIFIABLE
targets.source: T. Romanczukiewicz & Ya. Shnir, PRL 105, 081601 (2010), arXiv:1002.4484
targets.notes: Abstract-level only, via search summaries (PubMed and APS listings).

targets.quantity: Demidov & Levkov 2011: soliton pair production from particle collisions / classical wave packets
targets.value: PRL: semiclassical method; pair-production probability exponentially suppressed by a factor that is almost constant at high energies. Companion JHEP 06 (2011) 016 (arXiv:1103.2133): colliding wave packets characterized by energy E and particle number N; stochastic sampling over packet shapes maps the whole region of the (E,N) plane with classical pair creation. Boundary values, model potential and packet ansatz: UNVERIFIABLE
targets.notes: The snippets say '(1+1)-dimensional scalar field model'. I could not confirm it is plain phi4 (I recall a modified potential, unverified).

targets.quantity: Single-field Gaussian perturbations producing kink-antikink pairs in phi4 (closest analog to colliding single Gaussian packets)
targets.value: Simas & da Hora: Gaussian bump of amplitude A0 and width sigma added to the vacuum phi0 = +1. A0 = 0.60 decays into an antikink-kink pair plus a central small oscillon; A0 = 0.70 gives two nearly pure antikink-kink pairs; A0 near 1 gives composite multi-pair states. sigma and potential normalization UNVERIFIABLE. Older study (arXiv:1004.4643): depending on width, amplitude and energy, a Gaussian gives radiation, oscillons, kink-antikink pairs or shock waves. Unattributed snippet: 'beyond the threshold of four times the energy of the kink, a kink-antikink pair can appear'. Askari, Saadatmand, Dmitriev & Javidan, Wave Motion 78 (2018) 54, arXiv:1608.01847: colliding wave trains built from tanh differences, e.g. k = 2.25 with A = 0.15 and 0.1; max energy density in N-kink collisions = N^2/2 for even N
targets.source: F. C. Simas & E. da Hora, arXiv:2404.17848 (Annals of Physics 2025); arXiv:1004.4643; arXiv:1608.01847
targets.notes: No source found giving a sharp production threshold for two colliding single Gaussian packets of phi itself. That map would be new work. Albayrak & Vachaspati (PRD 109, 036001, 2024; arXiv:2308.01962) use a second field with quantum mediation: production favored by large total energy, wide packets, low velocity.

targets.quantity: Rational-map initial conditions for Hopf solitons
targets.value: Map R^3 -> S^3: Z1 = (x1 + i x2) sin f(r)/r, Z0 = cos f(r) + i (x3/r) sin f(r), with f monotone, f(0) = pi, f(inf) = 0 (e.g. f = pi/(1 + r^2/r0^2)). Then W = n-field stereographic coordinate. Axial: W = Z1^n / Z0^m gives A_{n,m} with Q = n m. Torus knots (Sutcliffe 2007): W = Z1^alpha Z0^beta / (Z1^a + Z0^b), a,b coprime, a > b, alpha >= 1, beta >= 0, Q = alpha b + beta a; K_{a,b} has a(b-1) crossings. Trefoil K_{3,2}: Q=5 (alpha,beta) = (1,1), Q=6 (3,0), Q=7 (2,1) (derived from the Q formula)
targets.source: Torus-knot family and Q formula: search summary of arXiv:1707.06608 describing Sutcliffe's ansatz; Foster arXiv:1012.2595 confirms its use. The S^3 map and axial family are from recall, validated here (they produced Q=1 and Q=2 solitons with E = 1.23, 2.00)
targets.notes: Trefoil energies 53.09/57.20/61.32 that appeared in searches belong to the elastic-rod model, not Skyrme-Faddeev.

targets.quantity: Hedgehog Einstein-Skyrme field equations and coupling definition
targets.value: L = (f^2/4) Tr(d_mu U d^mu U^+) + (1/(32 e^2)) Tr([U^+ d_mu U, U^+ d_nu U]^2); U = exp(i sigma.rhat F(r)); ds^2 = -sigma(r)^2 N(r) dt^2 + dr^2/N + r^2 dOmega^2, N = 1 - 2m/x; x = e f r; alpha = 4 pi G f^2. m' = alpha [ N F'^2 (x^2/2 + sin^2F) + sin^2F (1 + sin^2F/(2x^2)) ]; sigma'/sigma = alpha (x + 2 sin^2F/x) F'^2; ( sigma N (x^2 + 2 sin^2F) F' )' = sigma sin2F ( N F'^2 + 1 + sin^2F/x^2 ). BCs: F(0) = pi, F(inf) = 0, m(0) = 0, sigma(inf) = 1. ADM mass M = (4 pi f/e) m(inf)/alpha

targets.quantity: Branch structure
targets.value: For alpha < alpha_crit there are two regular solutions. The lower (skyrmion) branch starts at the flat skyrmion at alpha = 0 and is stable. The upper branch is unstable and extends back to alpha -> 0, where (rescaled) it approaches the lowest Bartnik-McKinnon solution ('BM branch'). They merge at alpha_crit; none exist above it. Scaled mass decreases along both branches toward alpha_crit, with the minimum there
targets.source: Zajac arXiv:0906.4322; Dzhunushaliev et al. arXiv:2407.17504; Kleihaus-Kunz-Sood hep-th/9503087 (cusp at critical coupling); all via search summaries. A 2018 paper (arXiv:1803.09736) notes some erroneous statements in Bizon-Chmaj 1992
targets.notes: Own computation confirms two roots merging at alpha_crit.

PHI4 (A): velocities are invariant under rescaling x,t -> x/s,t/s, so v_c = 0.2598 and the window velocities hold for any (lam, v). Kink-antikink IC (kink at -x0 moving right at speed u, antikink at +x0 moving left, gamma = 1/sqrt(1-u^2)): phi(x,0) = v[tanh(gamma m (x+x0)/2) - tanh(gamma m (x-x0)/2) - 1]; phi_t(x,0) = -(v m gamma u/2)[sech^2(gamma m (x+x0)/2) + sech^2(gamma m (x-x0)/2)]. The background is -v outside and +v between the pair. Use half-separation x0 >~ 7-10 kink widths (the arXiv:2009.00355 snippet used a = 7). Window edges shift with separation and discretization (a Hartree-approximation paper notes this), so run a convergence check (dx in {0.05, 0.025}/(m/2), dt = 0.5 dx, leapfrog or RK4, large box or absorbing boundaries). Detect bounces from phi(0,t) sign changes; get the output velocity by tracking the kink centre. Resonance picture: windows indexed by n = number of shape-mode oscillations between bounces, T_n ~ (2 pi n + delta)/omega_s with omega_s = (sqrt3/2) m (delta and the n-offset UNVERIFIED). Suggested Gaussian-packet IC for the seed's experiment (our design, not from a source): phi = -v + sum over +- A exp(-(x -+ x0)^2/(2 sigma^2)) cos(k (x -+ x0)), with phi_t from the linear dispersion omega = sqrt(k^2 + m^2) (right-mover phi_t = +A omega e^{...} sin(k(x - x0)), mirrored for the left-mover). Scan (A, sigma, k); report energy in units of 2 M_kink. DSV used trains of N_b breather-like pulses at omega ~ 1, not single packets. No published sharp threshold for colliding single Gaussian packets of phi was found (Albayrak & Vachaspati 2026 report fractured, non-sharp production in 2D).

FADDEEV-SKYRME (C): use the Sutcliffe 2007 normalization E = (1/(32 sqrt2 pi^2)) Int [(d n)^2 + (1/2) sum_{i,j} (d_i n x d_j n)^2]; Ward bound c = 1, proven c = (3/16)^{3/8} = 0.534. Own axial check (scratchpad hopf_axial_m.py): ansatz (n1 + i n2)(rho,phi,z) = e^{i m phi}(n1 + i n2)(rho,0,z); L-BFGS on unconstrained v with n = v/|v|; hand-coded gradient verified by finite differences. Lessons: (i) a centred/averaged-difference stencil has checkerboard null modes, so the soliton unwinds (E -> 0.008); use a corner/edge stencil. (ii) In the axial reduction the 2 pi rho volume weight makes lattice defects on the symmetry axis nearly free; the core slipped onto the axis and unwound (E = 0.48, below the proven bound). Pin the axis nodes to n = e3 (legitimate for W = Z1^n/Z0). (iii) Hopf charge is not lattice-protected in 3D either: monitor that min n3 reaches -1, and check Q by the Whitehead integral (solve F = dA by FFT) or by preimage linking. Results: E1 = 1.231 (h = 0.08, box 8), E2 = 1.9995; Derrick ratio E2/E4 ~ 0.97-0.98, with the deviation due to the finite fixed-boundary box.

EINSTEIN-SKYRME (F): shoot from x0 = 1e-4 with F = pi - a x, m = 0. Bisect on a: overshoot (F crosses 0) vs undershoot (F' turns positive), DOP853 at rtol 1e-10. For fixed alpha there are two roots in a (lower/skyrmion branch near a ~ 2.0-2.8, upper branch at larger a). The fold is found by computing alpha(a) at fixed a, again by bisection, and maximizing it: alpha_crit = 0.040378 at a = 2.9303. A grid scan in a underestimates alpha_crit (gave 0.040328) because the merging roots fall between grid points. Convention check is essential: alpha = 4 pi G f^2 with L = (f^2/4)Tr(dU dU^+), i.e. f = F_pi(ANW)/2. Using F_pi(ANW) in place of f would shift alpha_crit by a factor of 4. Flat hedgehog via scipy solve_bvp with far BC F + x F'/2 = 0 (F ~ k/x^2) plus an analytic tail: E/(12 pi^2) = 1.23145.

Under A1~ = A1^3: 14 = 3 + 4 + 4 + 3 x 1 (the singlets are the long-root su(2) on 3a+2b). Under A1 + A1~ = so(4): 14 = (3,1) + (1,3) + (2,4).
targets.source: Mayanskiy arXiv:1611.04070, Proposition 4.1
targets.notes: Not read, my derivation: 7 = (2,2) + (1,3) under SU(2)_long x SU(2)_short, consistent with index ratio 1:3. For a long-root hedgehog, the 8 doublet directions all share one inertia by SU(2)_short symmetry; with Skyrme traces normalized as Tr_7/2 that inertia equals the SU(3) I2. The 3 short-root directions have zero inertia (they commute with U0). Without a WZ term, states must be right-SU(2)_short singlets.

targets.quantity: Known solutions: F2 hopfions and BPS sphalerons
targets.value: F2 Skyrme-Faddeev-Niemi hopfions come in two ansatz types: a trivial SU(2) embedding of CP1 hopfions, and a non-embedded configuration via Baecklund transformation. Both reduce exactly to the CP1 SFN Euler-Lagrange equations, and zero-mode quantization was done. Static analytic F2 NLSM solutions saturate E >= pi(|N_A| + |N_B| + |N_C|) with N_A + N_B + N_C = 0, but are saddle points ('BPS sphalerons'); topological charge Q = N_A - N_C.
targets.source: Amari & Sawado arXiv:1805.10008 (abstract, Sec. II-III); Amari & Sawado arXiv:1711.00933 (abstract, eq. (6), eq. (31))
targets.notes: For the energy ladder E_Q/E_1, the F2 hopfion energies in these ansatze equal the CP1 SFN ones in the corresponding units.

SKYRME CONVENTIONS AND FORMULAS:
- The ANW Lagrangian is (F_pi^2/16) Tr(dU dU^dag) + (1/(32 e^2)) Tr[L_mu, L_nu]^2, with F_pi = 186 MeV experimental (f_pi = F_pi/2). ANW fit: F_pi = 129 MeV, e = 5.45.
- Use the dimensionless radius x = e F_pi r (Schechter-Weigel use x = e f_pi r; take care with the factor 2).
- Energy (ANW): M = 4 pi (F_pi/e) int dx x^2 [ (1/8)(F'^2 + 2 s^2/x^2) + (1/2)(s^2/x^2)(s^2/x^2 + 2F'^2) ], with s = sinF.
- Euler-Lagrange equation in these units: (x^2/4 + 2s^2) F'' = (1/2) s c + 2 s^3 c/x^2 - 2 s c F'^2 - (1/2) x F', with c = cosF.
- Boundary conditions: F(0) = pi. For massless pions do NOT impose F(X) = 0. Impose F'(X) + 2F(X)/X = 0 and add analytic tails: C^2/X for Lambda and C^2/(2X) for the I2 integral, where C = F(X) X^2. Forcing F(60) = 0 gave Lambda = 48.7 instead of 51.0. The inertia integrals converge only like 1/X.
- I1 = lambda = (2pi/3)(1/(e^3 F_pi)) int x^2 s^2 [1 + 4(F'^2 + s^2/x^2)]. The task's 'lambda = 50.9/(e^3 F_pi)' omits 2pi/3.
- I2 = (pi/2)(1/(e^3 F_pi)) int x^2 (1-c) [1 + F'^2 + 2 s^2/x^2] (Kopeliovich hep-th/9707067, eq. 22c).
- Isoscalar radius: <r^2>_{I=0} = -(2/pi) int r^2 s^2 F' dr.
- Magnetic moments (nuclear magnetons): mu_{p,n} = 2 M_N [ <r^2>_{I=0}/(12 lambda) +- lambda/6 ].
- g_A = -(pi/(3e^2)) int x^2 [F' + sin2F/x + 4(sin2F F'^2/x + 2 s^2 F'/x^2 + s^2 sin2F/x^3)].
- g_piNN = 2 M_N g_A / F_pi (Goldberger-Treiman, 186-convention).
- Sanity checks: M/(3 pi^2 F_pi/e) = 1.2315; F'(0) = -1.004 in x = e F_pi r units.
- Ma-Harada (1604.04850) analytic magnetic-moment formulas are fine, but their numerical coefficients disagree with the ANW normalization; do not calibrate against them.

SU(3) ROTOR:
- E = M + C2(p,q)/(2 I2) + (1/(2I1) - 1/(2I2)) J(J+1) - Nc^2/(24 I2), with C2 = (p^2 + q^2 + pq + 3p + 3q)/3 (DPP eq. 8; Praszalowicz eq. 3).
- Constraint Y_R = Nc B/3 = 1: allowed irreps contain Y = 1 states, and J equals their isospin.
- Splittings: 3/(2I1) for 10-8 and 3/(2I2) for 10bar-8.
- Charges: Q = I3 + Y/2 with Y = 2 L8/sqrt3 (left generators).
- Symmetry breaking (for mass splittings): H' = -alpha D88 (plus beta Y and gamma D8i S_i terms in chiQSM).
- Praszalowicz gives second-order matrix elements, Delta_{R'R} = C2(R') - C2(R), and the delta coefficients (hep-ph/0308114, eqs. 13-19).

PI0 ANOMALY:

- PDG 2026: Gamma(gamma gamma) = hbar BR/tau = 7.72 +- 0.12 eV, with hbar = 6.582119569e-22 MeV s.
- PrimEx-II: 7.802 +- 0.117 eV.

G2 (my derivations, no literature found):
- Normalize Skyrme traces in the 7 as Tr_7/2. This reproduces SU(2) for the long-root embedding and SU(3) for SU(3) inside G2 (7 = 3 + 3bar + 1).
- Long-root hedgehog: inertia splits as 3 x I1 + 8 x I2 + 3 zero modes. The 8 doublet directions have I2 equal to the SU(3) value by SU(2)_short symmetry; the zero modes are the commutant SU(2)_short, which requires right-SU(2)_short singlets because there is no WZ term.
- In long-root normalization: T(7) = 1, C2(7) = 2, C2(14) = h-dual = 4.
- Rotor (my derivation): H = J(J+1)/(2I1) + [C2(R) - J(J+1)]/(2I2) on states whose right SU(2)_short content is trivial.
- Branching: 14 = (3,1) + (1,3) + (2,4) (read); 7 = (2,2) + (1,3) (derived).

F21 BASIS:
- D = diag(zeta, zeta^2, zeta^4) and C = [[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[1,0,0]] satisfy C D C^-1 = D^2 and C^-1 D C = D^4. This matches LNR's d^-1 c d = c^4 and King-Luhn's T7 generators.
- LNR's PSL(2,7) triplet (0709.1447, eqs. 22-23) contains both D and C. I checked: order 168, invariant xy^3 + yz^3 + zx^3.
